zh_keywords: 穿刺|活检|取样|穿刺是什么|prostate biopsy|怎么取
lay_explanation_en: A prostate biopsy takes small tissue samples (cores) from the prostate with a thin needle, and a pathologist examines them under the microscope. It is a sampling test: it can confirm cancer when cancer is in the sampled tissue, but it cannot examine the whole gland, so a normal result does not completely exclude cancer.
safety_netting_en: If anything about the result or the procedure is unclear, ask the treating urologist to walk through the report core by core.
sources: probiopsy (ProBIOPSY consensus, Chernysheva et al., Eur Urol 2026); eau_guideline (EAU Prostate Cancer Guidelines, uroweb.org, living guideline)

zh_keywords: 为什么要穿刺|建议穿刺|需要穿刺吗|psa升高|mri异常|医生让穿刺
lay_explanation_en: A biopsy is usually advised when something raises suspicion: a rising or elevated PSA blood test, an abnormal digital rectal examination, or an MRI that shows a suspicious area. Only a biopsy can obtain tissue, confirm whether cancer is present, and determine the grade group that guides later treatment decisions.
safety_netting_en: Whether and when to biopsy depends on age, other health problems, PSA density and MRI findings - discuss the personal trade-off with the treating urologist before deciding.
sources: probiopsy (ProBIOPSY consensus, Chernysheva et al., Eur Urol 2026); eau_guideline (EAU Prostate Cancer Guidelines, uroweb.org, living guideline); aua_part1_2022 (Eastham et al., AUA/ASTRO Guideline, J Urol 2022)

topic_en: A benign report is not a lifelong clearance
topic_zh: 穿刺良性不等于终身无癌
zh_keywords: 良性|穿刺结果是良性|良性还需要|阴性|不用管了|以后还要查|还用查psa|停止复查|终身|negative biopsy|benign result
en_keywords: benign|negative biopsy|do i still need|stop psa|follow-up
lay_explanation_en: A benign (negative) report means no cancer was found in the samples that were taken. It does not mean the prostate is free of cancer for life: small or hidden tumours can be missed by sampling, and some abnormalities can develop or progress later. This is why PSA blood tests and physical examinations should continue on the schedule the urologist gives, and MRI or a repeat biopsy may be recommended if suspicion stays high.
safety_netting_en: Keep the follow-up appointments and PSA tests even if you feel well; if PSA rises again or new symptoms appear, contact the treating urologist rather than waiting for the next scheduled visit.
sources: probiopsy (ProBIOPSY consensus, Chernysheva et al., Eur Urol 2026); eau_guideline (EAU Prostate Cancer Guidelines, uroweb.org, living guideline); borghesi_comp (Borghesi et al., complications after prostate biopsy, Eur Urol 2017)

topic_zh: 报告中的高级别上皮内瘤变（HGPIN）
zh_keywords: 高级别上皮内瘤变|hgpin|上皮内瘤变|异型增生|pin
lay_explanation_en: HGPIN means the cells lining the prostate ducts look abnormal under the microscope, but no cancer was found. It is not cancer and not a premalignant lesion that requires immediate surgery. With modern extended biopsy schemes, isolated HGPIN generally does not require an early repeat biopsy when no other suspicious findings are present - large studies show the cancer risk after isolated HGPIN is close to that of the general biopsy population - but PSA follow-up should continue as planned.
safety_netting_en: Ask the treating urologist whether your HGPIN was isolated and whether your MRI findings allow routine follow-up; attend every scheduled PSA check.
sources: hgpin_bju_2022 (management of isolated HGPIN, BJU Int 2022, doi:10.1111/bju.15568); eau_guideline (EAU Prostate Cancer Guidelines, uroweb.org, living guideline)

topic_zh: 报告中的非典型小腺泡增生（ASAP）
zh_keywords: 非典型小腺泡增生|asap|不典型小腺泡|异型腺体|非典型增生|atypical
lay_explanation_en: ASAP means the pathologist saw a tiny group of glands that look atypical - suspicious for cancer but not enough tissue to confirm it. Unlike isolated HGPIN, ASAP deserves attention: when men with ASAP are re-biopsied, a clinically significant cancer is found in a meaningful fraction, so urologists usually recommend an early repeat biopsy, often with MRI guidance targeting the same region.
safety_netting_en: Do not delay the repeat biopsy the urologist recommends; if MRI has not been done or is older than the biopsy, ask whether a fresh mpMRI should precede it.
sources: asap_rate_2024 (clinically significant cancer on repeat biopsy after ASAP, Oncology 2024, doi:10.1159/000535123); eau_guideline (EAU Prostate Cancer Guidelines, uroweb.org, living guideline)

zh_keywords: 怕疼|疼痛|疼不疼|痛不痛|不敢穿刺|害怕|麻醉|局麻|紧张|恐惧
lay_explanation_en: Fear of pain is common and worth raising openly. Prostate biopsy is normally performed with local anaesthesia - periprostatic nerve block is standard for both transrectal and transperineal routes - and the transperineal route can be done entirely under local anaesthetic. Most men tolerate the procedure well; discomfort is usually brief pressure rather than sharp pain. Avoiding a medically indicated biopsy out of fear can delay the diagnosis of a curable cancer, so tell the care team about the anxiety - sedation options and extra local anaesthetic can often be arranged.
safety_netting_en: Tell the treating team about the fear before the procedure day so anaesthesia can be planned; if the fear feels overwhelming, say so - it is a medical consideration, not an embarrassment.
sources: probiopsy (ProBIOPSY consensus, Chernysheva et al., Eur Urol 2026); bryant_translate (TRANSLATE RCT, Bryant et al., Lancet Oncol); yang_tps_meta (transperineal vs transrectal RCT meta-analysis, Eur Urol Open Sci)

zh_keywords: 穿刺前|准备|注意什么|抗凝|抗血小板|阿司匹林|利伐沙班|泻药|灌肠|抗生素|停药
lay_explanation_en: Before a biopsy the care team will normally review medications (especially blood thinners such as aspirin, clopidogrel or the newer oral anticoagulants - these are only ever changed on doctor's orders), give antibiotic prophylaxis according to local protocol, and may ask for bowel preparation. Bring the full medication and allergy list to the appointment.
safety_netting_en: Never stop blood thinners on your own - ask the prescribing doctor first; report all allergies and previous infections to the team beforehand.
sources: eau_guideline (EAU Prostate Cancer Guidelines, uroweb.org, living guideline); borghesi_comp (Borghesi et al., complications after prostate biopsy, Eur Urol 2017)

topic_zh: 穿刺后需要就医的情况
zh_keywords: 穿刺后|术后|发烧|发热|出血|尿血|便血|血尿|排不出尿|尿潴留|寒战|就医|急诊
lay_explanation_en: After a biopsy it is common to see blood in the urine for a few days, blood in the semen for several weeks, and light rectal bleeding. Genuine warning signs are different: fever with chills or shivering, heavy or persistent bleeding, inability to pass urine, or worsening pain - these can signal infection or bleeding that needs prompt treatment and should be reported the same day.
safety_netting_en: Contact the clinic or urgent care immediately for fever with chills, heavy bleeding, inability to urinate, or worsening pain; keep the clinic's after-procedure instruction sheet at hand.
sources: borghesi_comp (Borghesi et al., complications after prostate biopsy, Eur Urol 2017); eau_guideline (EAU Prostate Cancer Guidelines, uroweb.org, living guideline)

zh_keywords: 阳性|癌|腺癌|格里森|gleason|分级|分组|isup|评级|结果什么时候|多久出结果
lay_explanation_en: A positive report states whether cancer is present and assigns an ISUP grade group (from the Gleason pattern) - this grade, together with PSA and MRI, drives which treatments are suitable. Pathology processing takes days to about two weeks depending on the laboratory; the urologist will usually discuss the result in a dedicated appointment and lay out the treatment options.
safety_netting_en: Before the results appointment, write down the questions that matter to you (grade group, curability, treatment options); ask the urologist to explain the grade group in plain words.
sources: probiopsy (ProBIOPSY consensus, Chernysheva et al., Eur Urol 2026); aua_part1_2022 (Eastham et al., AUA/ASTRO Guideline, J Urol 2022)

zh_keywords: 要不要穿刺|犹豫|不想穿刺|有必要吗|过度检查|必须做吗|第二个意见|second opinion
lay_explanation_en: A biopsy decision is shared between patient and doctor: it weighs the chance of finding a significant cancer against age, other illnesses, anxiety, and the small risk of complications. It is reasonable to ask the urologist what happens with each choice - biopsy now, or active monitoring - and a second opinion on the indications is normal and acceptable.
safety_netting_en: If unsure, ask the treating urologist to explain what the PSA density and MRI say about the risk, and what the plan would be in either scenario; bring a family member to the consultation if helpful.
sources: probiopsy (ProBIOPSY consensus, Chernysheva et al., Eur Urol 2026); aua_part1_2022 (Eastham et al., AUA/ASTRO Guideline, J Urol 2022)
